prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, enabling measurement of time at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks meet the criterion I take most seriously: a discovery or invention with a named origin and a demonstrated payoff. Katori's magic-wavelength proposal removed the light-shift limit on trapping many neutral atoms. Ye's group then pushed the systematics and the many-body physics to roughly 1e-18, which made millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy practical. It is mature, because several independent laboratories reproduce the performance and international comparisons are routine, and it is not premature, because the redefinition of the second is being prepared. The two-person attribution fits the supplied names without leaving anyone obvious out. B015 also has the broadest top-of-ballot support in the room, with two first places and four top-three rankings from members with quite different fields. After reading the openings I place it above my own first choice, B013, for that reason.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the overlap with the 2005 prize, which honoured Hall and Haensch for the frequency comb, and with the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems, which included ion-trap clock-relevant technology. The committee will need a citation that clearly separates the lattice-clock concept from those earlier awards. A second reservation is that single-ion clocks and the Paris and PTB groups reached comparable uncertainties by other routes, so the credit is cleaner for the concept than for the record accuracies. Finally, the SI redefinition has not yet happened, and some members may prefer to wait for it.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B015 first and sees Katori as originator of the lattice-clock concept and Ye as the person who took strontium clocks to record accuracy, a mature field with a stable interpretation.
responses.response: I agree with the division of credit and with the maturity argument, and it is the main reason I now put B015 first. I would qualify the framing, though. Because of 2005 and 2012, the citation should name the invention of the lattice clock and its realization at 1e-18, not frequency metrology in general. I also do not want Ye's many-body and gravitational-redshift results to be read as a separate discovery. They show what the Katori concept made possible, which is a point for the pair rather than for adding a third name.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks the KPZ universality class (B023) first. He argues that Kardar and Zhang wrote the equation and Takeuchi supplied the decisive experimental confirmation, and that the field is conceptually deep and reaches into random-matrix statistics.
responses.response: I accept that KPZ is conceptually deep and that the Takeuchi experiments are a real confirmation. My difficulty is attribution. Mehlig's own opening notes that the exact solutions, which gave the Tracy-Widom statistics that make the story compelling, came from mathematical physicists who are not among the credited names. The committee would be honouring the 1986 equation and one experiment while the part that made it a precise universality class belongs to others. That is a harder allocation problem than lattice clocks. It is also only B023's single first-place vote, so the support does not show that the committee shares his weighting. I would like to hear whether he sees a configuration that credits the exact solutions fairly.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks twisted bilayer graphene (B006) first as a clean theory-plus-experiment case, a prediction followed by a surprise, while admitting that the field is young and the superconducting mechanism is unresolved.
responses.response: I rank B006 third and take the originality seriously. Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and Jarillo-Herrero's group found the correlated and superconducting states. The two other members who mention maturity (Kroll and Eriksson) also flag the open mechanism. The correlated phases are still being sorted out, and I would not want the citation to commit to an interpretation we may have to retract. I also see a credit risk in the 2018 experimental team, since Cao and colleagues are not among the credited names. With lattice clocks the open questions do not touch the core claim. If colleagues judge the interpretation sufficiently settled, B006 is my first alternative and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, ranks the IceCube discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (B007) first, stressing the diffuse flux, the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane result, while acknowledging that a collaboration of hundreds makes a three-person split somewhat arbitrary.
responses.response: The scientific case is strong. A new observational window is the type of discovery the prize exists for. I share his worry about attribution, and it is the reason I do not put B007 first: with Halzen, Karle and Spiering the committee would be choosing among many people who built the detector and the analyses, and AMANDA and Baikal also had a role. I would like the chair to say how the committee can justify the three names to the public. If that can be answered convincingly, I would support B007 as a serious contender in later rounds, even though it is not among my alternatives now.

uncertainties: Whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes leave enough room for a lattice-clock citation, and how to word it so the invention of the lattice clock is clearly distinct from the frequency comb.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the SI redefinition of the second before honouring optical clocks.
Whether the single-ion and Paris/PTB clock contributions are adequately represented by crediting only Katori and Ye.
How much weight B013 and B006 deserve if colleagues give more weight to field-defining breadth than to measurement precision.
statement.conflict_note: My opening first choice, B013 (aberration-corrected electron optics), is in my own field of transmission electron microscopy. I have no documented personal connection to Rose, Urban or Haider in my profile, but my professional proximity to the method means I should not be the deciding voice on it, and I have moved it to an alternative. Göran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague. His opening interest, B024, does not involve my own work, so no specific conflict is apparent for the preferred configuration B015.
